# Disagreement Log — Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 17

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 33

---

## Disagreements

**v. 1** — "hard to tell" (EMET) vs. "hard to describe" (LOGOS) vs. "too great to put into words" (PNEUMA). Greek δυσδιήγητα = difficult to narrate/describe. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 2** — "fetters of darkness" (EMET) vs. "chains of darkness" (LOGOS, PNEUMA). Greek δεσμοῖς = bonds/chains/fetters. LOGOS/PNEUMA preferred.

**v. 2** — "exiles from eternal providence" (EMET) vs. "banished from eternal providence" (LOGOS) vs. "cut off from the eternal light of your providence" (PNEUMA — adds "light," not in text). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 3** — "scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness" (EMET) vs. "scattered beneath a dark curtain of forgetfulness" (LOGOS) vs. "swallowed in a black fog of forgetting" (PNEUMA). "curtain" better than "veil" for σκότει. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "inner chamber that held them" (EMET) vs. "inner room that contained them" (LOGOS) vs. "rooms where they hid" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "crashing sounds full of dread rang around them" (EMET) vs. "sounds full of dread rang around them" (LOGOS) vs. "sounds crashed around them — sounds filled with dread" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 4** — "gloomy phantoms with sullen faces" (EMET) vs. "grim phantoms with sullen faces" (LOGOS) vs. "gloomy shapes with sullen, scowling faces" (PNEUMA — adds "scowling"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 6** — "only an automatic fire shone through to them" (EMET, literal) vs. "an eerie fire that ignited itself" (LOGOS) vs. "a single unnatural fire, spontaneous and terrifying" (PNEUMA). Greek αὐτόματος πῦρ = spontaneous/self-kindled fire. LOGOS's rendering is clearest. SOPHIA adopts LOGOS.

**v. 6** — "deemed the things they saw to be worse than that sight which was not seen" (EMET, literal) vs. "considered what they saw worse than the vision they could not see" (LOGOS) vs. "decided that what they could see was worse than what they could not" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 7** — "mockeries of their magic art were brought low" (EMET) vs. "tricks of their magic art were exposed for what they were" (LOGOS) vs. "clever tricks of their sorcerers were exposed as frauds" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "tricks of their magic art were exposed as worthless."

**v. 7** — "boasted wisdom was a reproach" (EMET) vs. "boasted wisdom was put to shame" (LOGOS) vs. "boasted wisdom collapsed into humiliation" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 8** — "ridiculous fear" (EMET) vs. "ridiculous terror" (LOGOS) vs. "ridiculous, uncontrollable terror" (PNEUMA — adds "uncontrollable"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 9** — "if nothing frightening disturbed them" (EMET) vs. "if nothing alarming actually threatened them" (LOGOS) vs. "when nothing genuinely threatening was near them" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 9** — "passing of beasts" (EMET) vs. "passing of reptiles" (LOGOS) vs. "slithering of reptiles" (PNEUMA). Greek ἑρπετῶν = reptiles/crawling things. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 10** — "perished trembling, refusing to see even the air" (EMET) vs. "perished trembling, refusing to look even at the air" (LOGOS) vs. "died trembling, too afraid to look at the air itself" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 10** — "could not be escaped on any side" (EMET) vs. "could not escape no matter which way they turned" (LOGOS) vs. "could not be escaped" (PNEUMA abbreviated). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 11** — "wickedness is a coward" (PNEUMA) vs. "wickedness is cowardly" (LOGOS) vs. "wickedness is a coward" (EMET). LOGOS: "cowardly" is the adjective form, slightly smoother.

**v. 11** — "condemned by its own testimony" (EMET) vs. "condemned by its own witness" (LOGOS) vs. "condemns itself with its own inner voice" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "condemned by its own inner witness."

**v. 11** — "magnifies misfortunes" (EMET) vs. "imagines the worst" (LOGOS) vs. "imagines disaster worse than it is" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 12** — "surrender of the resources that come from reason" (EMET) vs. "abdication of the help that comes from reason" (LOGOS) vs. "giving up of reason's defenses" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 13** — All three struggle with the compressed Greek. EMET: "the expectation from within, being less, counts the ignorance more than the cause of the torment." LOGOS: "the inner expectation, being deficient, reckons its ignorance as worse than the cause of the suffering." PNEUMA paraphrases the argument. LOGOS preferred.

**v. 14** — "powerless night" vs. "that night — powerless as it was" — LOGOS interpolates "powerless as it was" for clarity. SOPHIA retains LOGOS structure.

**v. 15** — "driven by monstrous apparitions" (EMET, LOGOS) vs. "driven now by monstrous, lurching apparitions" (PNEUMA — adds "lurching"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 15** — "paralyzed by their soul's surrender" (EMET) vs. "paralyzed by the collapse of their own souls" (LOGOS) vs. "paralyzed as their own souls gave way beneath them" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 16** — "kept under guard, shut up in a prison not made of iron" (EMET) vs. "kept prisoner, shut up in a jail not made of iron" (LOGOS) vs. "held down, imprisoned, as if by bars of iron, though no iron was there" (PNEUMA — inverts). EMET/LOGOS agree; SOPHIA: EMET form.

**v. 17** — "inescapable fate" (EMET) vs. "inescapable doom" (LOGOS) vs. "doom from which there was no escape" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 17** — "single chain of darkness" (LOGOS, PNEUMA) vs. "same chain of darkness" (EMET). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 18** — "rhythm of rushing water" (EMET) vs. "steady rushing of water" (LOGOS) vs. "rhythmic sound of rushing water" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "the rhythmic sound of rushing water."

**v. 19** — "unseen running of leaping animals" (EMET) vs. "unseen galloping of leaping animals" (LOGOS) vs. "unseen galloping of some leaping animal in the dark" (PNEUMA — adds "in the dark"). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 19** — "savage roaring beasts" (EMET) vs. "fierce wild beasts" (LOGOS) vs. "full-throated roar of a wild beast" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 20** — "illuminated with brilliant light" (EMET) vs. "bathed in brilliant light" (LOGOS) vs. "flooded with brilliant light" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 20** — "conducted its work unhindered" (EMET) vs. "went about its work unimpeded" (LOGOS) vs. "going about its business without interruption" (PNEUMA). LOGOS preferred.

**v. 21** — "an image of the darkness that was to receive them" (EMET) vs. "a foretaste of the darkness destined to receive them" (LOGOS) vs. "a foretaste, an image of the darkness that was already waiting" (PNEUMA). SOPHIA: "an image of the darkness destined to receive them" — retaining EMET's "image" with LOGOS's "destined."
